about: What a trip's stored figures must be, computed from its legs. The legs are the record of what was actually driven; total_distance_km, odometer_distance_km, estimated_cost, primary_mode and cost_basis are all derived from them and must never be typed or left behind. Both apps write trips, so both implement this and both test suites read this file.
why: Found on 25 August 2026 from TRP-00311. A leg was created as 'Own Vehicle' (Rs 7/km), stored 53 x 7 = 371, and later edited to 'Bike' (Rs 3.5/km). Nothing recomputed the stored cost, so the trip claimed 371 against 185.50 actually earned - exactly double. Four of Prasad V's trips are in that state. Separately, five of Prashanth's read as stale only because the dashboard was ignoring claimed_amount on Mixed legs; those stored figures were right all along.

rates.note: Trip Rate Settings on the live site. rate_company is vestigial - a Company Vehicle trip prices at rate_company_car / rate_company_bike, which are the fields read.

rules.rate_follows_the_leg: Money comes from each leg's own mode, never from Trip.primary_mode. The header is derived FROM the legs, so it can never disagree with what was charged.
rules.own_vehicle_means_car: 'Own Vehicle' prices at the own-CAR rate. A rep on their own motorbike must be recorded as 'Bike' or they are paid double - this is the mistake TRP-00311 is.
rules.mixed_adds_the_fare: A Mixed leg earns distance x rate PLUS its claimed_amount. The claimed amount is a ticket - a bus or train fare that is not per kilometre - and dropping it zeroes a real claim. A Mixed leg with no distance is a fare and nothing else.
rules.claimed_amount_only_on_mixed: Every other mode is paid per kilometre alone. claimed_amount on a Bike leg is not added, or the rep is paid twice for the same journey.
rules.primary_mode_from_legs: No legs: leave it alone, the stored value is at least what the rep chose. One distinct mode: that mode. More than one: 'Mixed'.
rules.cost_basis: 'Odometer' when any leg carries odometer distance, otherwise 'GPS Distance'.

totals.why: TRP-00311 as it should have been read once the leg said Bike - the case this rule was written for
the same distance recorded as Own Vehicle earns exactly double - which is why the two must never be confused
a Mixed leg with no distance is a bus fare and nothing else - five of Prashanth's trips are exactly this, and reading them as zero would take Rs 1088 off one of them
a Mixed leg that was both driven and ticketed earns both halves
a claimed amount on a non-Mixed leg is ignored - paying it would pay the rep twice for one journey
two modes on one day make the header Mixed, and each leg is still paid at its own rate
a leg without an odometer still counts towards the distance, but not towards the odometer figure - and with none of them the basis is GPS
one leg with an odometer is enough to make the whole trip odometer-based
a company vehicle earns nothing per kilometre - the company already paid for the fuel
an unrecognised mode earns nothing rather than guessing a rate, and still counts its distance
no legs leaves primary_mode to the caller - there is nothing to derive it from, and the stored value is at least what the rep chose
